transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-05
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Kim (Redwood CSM); Marcus Chen, Priya Nair, Ethan Walsh, Sofia Morales (HeliosGrid)

Summary:
Quick partner intro between Redwood and HeliosGrid to scope integration patterns (resell vs referral vs onramp), private deployment requirements (VPC/VPN, KMS/HSM), and a concrete benchmarking pilot to validate latency/cost tradeoffs on HeliosGrid workloads. Action items and follow-ups agreed.

Topics:
- Partner business model options (reseller, OEM, referral)
- Technical integration: private plane, VPC peering, on-prem connector
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, RBAC, audit logs, SAML SSO
- Performance: quantization, batching, kernel tuning, KV cache behavior
- Next steps: benchmark, docs, pricing/SOW

References shared during meeting:
- Redwood partner integration doc (link): https://redwood.ai/partner-integration
- Benchmark spreadsheet (HeliosGrid): https://drive.company/heliosgrid/benchmarks (Helios internal)
- Demo recording template: https://redwood.ai/demo-template

Transcript:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Aisha, I'm the partner AE at Redwood — um, excited to meet the HeliosGrid team. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Marcus: Yeah, Marcus here, VP Cloud at HeliosGrid. We run a managed hybrid cloud for media workloads, and we're exploring deeper GPU partnerships.
[00:18] Priya: Priya — head of infra. We're especially interested in inference on customer data with strict residency so private deployments matter.
[00:25] Diego: Diego, SE at Redwood. I'll dig into the technical constraints, perf and configs we might need to run on your infra.
[00:32] Sofia: Sofia, platform eng — I own the integration hooks and deployment automation.
[00:36] Ethan: Ethan, procurement, I'll handle commercial timelines.
[00:40] Aisha: Thanks. Outline for today: 1) partner models, 2) security posture, 3) technical feasibility, 4) propose pilot and benchmarks. Ok?
[00:48] Marcus: Sounds good.

[01:05] Diego: Quick high level on how Redwood serves models — we have hosted API, dedicated reserved pools and private deploys. For private, we provide a control plane that can live in your VPC or on-prem; customers can run inference in your network and we can integrate KMS for key wrapping.
[01:22] Priya: When you say control plane in our VPC, do you mean full control plane or just a management agent? We have strict network segmentation; needs to be air-gapped for some customers.
[01:31] Diego: Yeah — so we have two patterns. One is a lightweight control plane that talks back over a spec'ed TLS channel to Redwood for licensing/metrics; the other is fully air-gapped on-prem bundle. The latter is heavier but meets regulatory needs.
[01:45] Priya: Ok, that second option is interesting — do you support HSM/KMS integrations? We encrypt at rest and in motion and want the keys kept in our HSM.
[01:53] Diego: Absolutely, we support KMS providers and HSM. There might be some additional work for customer-managed HSM connectors but it's supported.

[02:10] Marcus: From a partner model, are you looking for a reseller relationship where we host Redwood for customers, or a channel referral? What's typical?
[02:19] Aisha: We do both. Reseller / managed service partners typically get different pricing bands and a partner SOW; referral is lighter weight. For HeliosGrid's model — if you want to offer a Redwood-backed inference add-on, reseller makes sense. We can share the SOW template.
[02:32] Marcus: Good. We'll want margins and co-marketing. Also curious on how you handle billing reconciliation if we host dedicated GPUs and Redwood supplies the runtime.
[02:41] Aisha: We have flexible billing — either usage-based with a reserved commit or an MSRP+partner discount flow. We'll send sample bands after the call.

[03:00] Sofia: Technical question about the runtime — how does Redwood handle KV cache and prefix caching when you run many multi-tenant jobs? We saw issues with cache eviction on other runtimes.
[03:12] Diego: Our runtime has per-tenant KV caches and smart eviction heuristics. There's also a continuous batching layer that groups similar seq length requests to keep latency predictable. In practice we tune the kernel selection based on sequence distribution — some folks call that kernel sel, or kernel pickers.
[03:30] Priya: You said kernel selection, is that automatic or do we need to rebuild kernels per customer?
[03:35] Diego: Mostly automatic; for very specific quantized models we may recommend a compile step. But 90% of the time the runtime auto-selects the best kernel.

[03:52] Marcus: Performance — we need <60ms P95 for short prompt completions for some customers. Can you hit that on our GPU stack? We're running A100-ish equivalents and some Ampere variants.
[04:03] Diego: With our continuous batching disabled for ultra-low latency mode and beefy GPUs, hitting sub-60ms p95 for 128-token completions is possible with smaller models or compiled kernels. With larger models (>7B), you typically see higher latencies unless you shard or use quantization.
[04:18] Sofia: Are you recommending quantization like int8 or 4-bit? How does that affect quality for our media-processing LLM prompts?
[04:25] Diego: We can recommend quantization profiles per model. For many use cases int8 keeps quality high; for aggressive cost constraints we provide 4-bit profiles but you'd want to run a quality eval. Redwood Optimize also suggests per-workload quantization.

[04:45] Marcus: Security — SOC 2, audit logs, RBAC, SSO — all must be on the table. Does Redwood have SOC two and granular audit trails?
[04:53] Aisha: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II. We also have structured audit logs with per-token tracing available in the Console and RBAC via SAML SSO. We'll drop the SOC 2 packet in the shared folder.
[05:05] Priya: Do you store logs or PII by default? Our customers require minimal retention and the ability to turn off telemetry.
[05:12] Lena: We support configurable retention and can disable logging for sensitive customers; for private deployments you'll control retention policies.

[05:30] Ethan: Procurement — to move to a pilot, what does the contracting cadence look like? We have standard SLAs to review.
[05:36] Aisha: For pilots we usually work off a partner pilot addendum and a short SOW. For production reseller contracts we'll align on revenue share and support tiers. We'll send a pilot SOW template after this call.

[06:00] Sophia: We want to run a benchmark with our real telemetry. What's a good shape for that benchmark? QPS, latency, and cost per 1M tokens?
[06:09] Diego: Good question. We recommend a 2-hour steady-state run with your representative request distribution: 1) short completions (<=128 tokens) for interactive paths, 2) medium (256-512) for batch jobs. We'll measure P50/P95/P99 latency, GPU utilization, and tokens/sec. We can also run with different quantization and batching knobs.
[06:28] Marcus: Great. We'll need a config doc for the benchmark environment so we can replicate.
[06:34] Diego: I'll attach a benchmark config guide — it includes the docker images, env vars, and profiles for the Redwood runtime.

[06:50] [crosstalk] Priya: — and what about network egress, does Redwood require broad outbound access?
[06:55] Diego: For the lightweight control plane we need a small set of TLS endpoints outbound, we can provide an allowlist. For air-gapped installs there's no outbound.

[07:10] Marcus: Any multi-tenancy restrictions if we host multiple customers on the same cluster?
[07:15] Diego: You can have multi-tenant pools with strong isolation — per-tenant KV, separate model sandboxes, and enforced RBAC. For high security customers we recommend dedicated pools per customer.

[07:30] Priya: For the private/offline bundle, what's the footprint? GPUs aside, is there a recommended disk or memory profile?
[07:38] Diego: Typical control plane + runtime needs 32-64GB RAM for the manager nodes and disk depends on model cache sizes. We'll send a sizing guide; if you plan to host many models cold caches could need multiple TBs.

[07:55] Marcus: On the partnership side, marketing and support — do you co-sell? Is there joint go-to-market?
[08:01] Aisha: Yes, we do co-marketing and provide partner enablement. We have partner portal materials and case study templates; margins vary by program.

[08:15] Sofia: One practical: we use an internal k8s flavour with custom CNI. Do you support operator-based installs or Helm only?
[08:23] Diego: We support both operator and Helm flavors. For very old k8s we have manifests. We'll work with your infra team to adapt.

[08:40] [laughter] Marcus: Ok now the tricky question: how do you handle graceful degradation if a model is slow or the pool is saturated? We need our customer-facing product to avoid 500s.
[08:50] Diego: We have smart routing policies — fallbacks to smaller model variants, circuit breakers, and autoscaling policies. For very critical flows you can configure automatic reroute to a cached completion or competitor model as fallback.
[09:05] Priya: Competitor fallback — is that out-of-the-box or a config thing?
[09:08] Diego: It's a policy config you enable; we can route to other available model endpoints or to a cached response.

[09:25] Marcus: Any red flags on our stack? We're using mixed GPU instances and plan to onboard customers globally.
[09:32] Diego: Mixed hardware adds complexity for predictable latency but our kernel selector helps. Global onboardings will need regional routing and optionally dedicated capacity in each region to meet SLOs.

[09:50] Aisha: Let's talk timeframes — what's your target to go-to-market with a Redwood-backed inference product?
[09:56] Marcus: We'd like a pilot in 3 weeks, production within 3 months — depending on procurement.
[10:02] Aisha: That seems reasonable. We'll aim to get the pilot plan and pricing to you within 4 business days.

[10:15] Sofia: One more tech point, do you support offline model imports and custom model packaging? Some of our customers want to bring their own weights.
[10:23] Diego: Yes, BYOM is supported. For private deployments you can bring model artifacts, we provide a model onboarding checklist that includes compatibility notes (quantization, ops).

[10:38] Priya: Regarding telemetry, can we have per-customer token-level cost breakdowns?
[10:44] Lena: Yes, Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. For private we can feed telemetry into your observability stack if needed.

[10:55] Ethan: Procurement: for the pilot we typically need a short SOW and PO. What are usual pilot terms? Is there a free eval?
[11:02] Aisha: We offer partner pilots with modest fee to cover infra; sometimes free for strategic partners. We'll propose a pilot cost and scope in the SOW.

[11:20] Marcus: Competitors — we've talked to AICore and CloudTitan. Why pick Redwood?
[11:27] Aisha: Our differentiator is production-first runtime + ops: predictable SLOs, cost controls (batching/quant profiles), and a unified API across hosted/dedicated/private. Also our partner program provides reseller pricing and enablement.

[11:45] [silence for 5s] Priya: Ok if we run the benchmark, what control plane telemetry do you need? We may want to scrub data.
[11:54] Diego: For the benchmark we need request samples (non-PII), traces for latency, and a token distribution. You can scrub any PII. We can sign an NDA or add data handling clauses.

[12:08] Marcus: Let's lock down the benchmark scope now — 2 hours, short/medium traffic, two model sizes (7B and 13B), int8 and fp16 runs?
[12:18] Diego: That works. We'll do int8 + fp16 and include a 4-bit run if you want to explore cost savings. We'll capture P50/P95/P99 and GPU util.

[12:33] Sofia: For the benchmark environment, do you want us to provision a dedicated cluster or can you use an agent that runs on our k8s?
[12:40] Diego: Either works. For fidelity, dedicated clusters on your hardware are best; agent-based runs are also fine if you prefer.

[12:55] Aisha: Quick recap of immediate next steps: we will share partner SOW template, SOC 2 packet, and the benchmark config; Diego will schedule the benchmark run with Priya/Sofia; procurement (Ethan) will get pilot billing terms.

[13:12] Ethan: Sounds good — can you also include a sample PO template?
[13:16] Aisha: Yep, sample PO and procurement checklist.

[13:28] Marcus: Any blockers you're seeing?
[13:31] Diego: Nothing major — the only potential blocker is any air-gapped requirement for certain customers; that pushes to the heavier on-prem bundle which has longer lead time.
[13:43] Marcus: Ok we have a few customers with strict offline needs but not for the pilot.

[14:00] Priya: Let's put a date on the technical deep dive — week of 2027-02-15?
[14:05] Aisha: Works for us. Diego, Lena — can you hold a 90-min deep dive then?
[14:10] Diego: Yes, I'll prepare runtime metrics and a demo of KV cache behavior.

[14:22] [brief aside] Sofia: Also, do you support model governance — ability to block specific outputs or filter certain tokens?
[14:29] Diego: We have content filters and output policies you can plug into the pipeline, plus structured function-calling to constrain outputs.

[14:44] Aisha: Anything else before we close?
[14:47] Marcus: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.

[15:00] Closing notes:
- Agreed pilot: 2-hour benchmark, models 7B & 13B, int8/fp16, measure latency & GPU util.
- Redwood to share: SOW template, SOC 2 packet, benchmark config, partner pricing bands, PO template.
- Schedule: benchmark within 1 week, deep dive week of 2027-02-15.

Action items (restate):
- Aisha Patel - Send partner integration checklist, SOW template and pricing bands (due 2027-02-09)
- Diego Ramos - Schedule benchmark and share config + agent images (due 2027-02-10)
- Priya Nair / Sofia Morales - Provide sample request traces and env access for benchmark (due 2027-02-08)
- Ethan Walsh - Provide procurement timeline and PO requirements (due 2027-02-12)

End of transcript.
